name: Money Buys Happiness | Chapter 2 Starter Guide
description_md:
Money Buys Happiness

>This series provides 10 playtested decks using the Chapter 2 Core and new Starters, with each deck compatible for two player with at least 7 others (and working well at high player counts). Here big money André makes it rain with [Marcus](/card/60375), [Sticky Fingers](/card/12048), [Thieves' Kit](/card/12049), [Emergency Cache](/card/01088), ["Watch this!"](/card/60371) and [Out the Door](/card/60370). He then puts this cash to work, with [Well Connected](/card/60381) for boosts and [Black Fan](/card/60379) for a raft of benefits. Don't believe what they say - money does buy happiness! `If you want to support my work, give it a like ❤︎ and a favorite ★ on here!`

Series Decks

|   Mystic   |   Rogue   |   Guardian   |   Survivor   |   Seeker   | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Marie | André | Tommy| Miguel | Carolyn | | Dexter | Trish | Daniela | Izzie | Joe |

At a Glance

>| Stats | | >|:---|:---| >| Clue-finding: |  ★★★★☆ | >| Consistency: |  ★★★★☆ | >| Enemy Management: |  ★★★☆☆ | >| Encounter Defense: |  ★★★★☆ | >| Survivability: |  ★★★☆☆ | >| Simplicity: |  ★★★★★ |

Overview

- Baby I got your money, don't you worry: This deck is all about making bank. [Marcus](/card/60375), [Sticky Fingers](/card/12048), [Thieves' Kit](/card/12049), [Emergency Cache](/card/01088), ["Watch this!"](/card/60371), [Out the Door](/card/60370) and André's own ability all give resources. This is 34% of the deck overall, so you'll see these cards a lot! [Prestidigitation](/card/12052) also provides discounts, and returns an empty Thieves' Kit to be used again - with André being a capable clue-finder. As the deck isn't especially expensive (your most expensive card costs just 3 resources), this allows the cheddar to pile up. - Money makes the world go round: Money switches on [Well Connected](/card/60381), as with 20 resources you can receive a +5 boost to any test once per round. This works wonders both with André's ability and against treacheries. That 20 resource mark also powers up the [The Black Fan](/card/60379), giving a +1 to all your stats, more health and sanity, *and* an extra action per turn. [Easy Street](/card/60369) is your final enabler, providing a big wild boost that plays nicely with André's "Know the..." signature cards. A single copy of [Silver Tongue](/card/12047) is in the deck to allow another use for your cash (upgraded to [its better version](/card/60380) in higher XP campaigns). - Clued in: With this deck you'll often pivot from [Thieves' Kit](/card/12049) and [Lockpicks](/card/60372) in your hands for early clue-finding, to [The Black Fan](/card/60379) and Lockpicks later (i.e. when [Well Connected](/card/60381) can pick up the slack and boost another investigate action). Lockpicks facilitate over-success, triggering [Lucky Cigarette Case](/card/12044) alongside your ability. This card draw then helps you find Black Fan and Well Connected, giving this deck a nice arc. Lucky Cigarette Case is therefore a key mulligan target, as card draw can be tricky without it. - Give 'em the slip: André's 5 Agility stat makes him a capable evader, especially with the many icons dotted through his deck. With André often getting an extra action per turn, this makes it easier to evade, move and then clue-find in those final two actions. You also have [Right Under Their Noses](/card/60368) to provide clues for evading itself. - Weakness: [Weight of the World](/card/60355) is a bit of a pain, but [Well Connected](/card/60381) saves you from failure on many tough tests. [Marcus Sengstacke](/card/60375) also provides horror soak, meaning you can shoulder it better than other decks. Thank you: [5argon](https://arkhamdb.com/user/profile/61394/5argon) and [their thumbnail tool](https://arkham-starter.com/tool/thumbnails); [Valentin1331](https://arkhamdb.com/user/profile/42890/Valentin1331) for his support over the years; the community creators of [Arkham.Build](https://www.patreon.com/c/arkhambuild/) ([Felix](https://spoettel.dev/)), [Arkham Cards](https://www.patreon.com/c/arkhamcards/) ([zzorba](https://www.reddit.com/user/zzorba/)) and [ArkhamDB](https://www.patreon.com/c/kamalisk/) ([kamalisk](https://www.reddit.com/user/kamalisk/)) - linking their Patreons!

Explain Yourself!

Big money is a no brainer for André. Honestly there's not too much that's surprising here and the deck does what it says on the tin. In terms of not taking [Olivier](/card/12046), firstly it's in the Trish deck and secondly - while Olivier is great - I do like that with [Marcus](/card/60375) your sanity soak is taken care of in a single card. I have however made an alternate version of the deck with Olivier for those who are keen - link in the next section. Regarding no damage dealing options, they require a lot of space and so can be a distraction on evader decks depending on the specific focus. I did find André's stat ratings tricky on this deck, so I wanted to explain these a little. Clue-finding is 4 ★ by dint of the actor's frequent extra action, meaning he can net 4 clues in a turn (or even 5 with [The Black Fan's](/card/60379) extra action). Despite somewhat inconsistent card draw, the 4 ★ consistency rating is due to André decently evading enemies and finding clues with or without his full engine in place - i.e. he's still consistently doing what the deck is designed to do. Enemy management is a 3 ★ as, although André is an above average evader, you're not shutting enemies down permanently like you do with a Guardian.

Campaign starter and planned progression

In terms of side deck, please follow this link for an Olivier variant of the deck. I do slightly prefer [Marcus Sengstacke](/card/60375) on this deck (makes you richer faster, and soaks horror), which is why I put [Olivier](/card/12046) on my Trish deck for this series - even so I thought I'd oblige! 0 XP deck is below (and link here): A recommended order of purchases/upgrades is: - [Lockpicks](/card/60361) → [Lockpicks •](/card/60372) - 1 x [Unexpected Courage](/card/12094) → 1 x [Well Connected](/card/54006) - 1 x [Unexpected Courage](/card/12094) → [The Black Fan](/card/60379)* - 1 x [Silver Tongue](/card/12047) → 1 x [Well Connected](/card/54006) - [Marcus Sengstacke](/card/60362) → [Marcus Sengstacke ••](/card/60375) *Alternatively you can have [The Black Fan](/card/60379) as your final upgrade (for your second copy of [Silver Tongue](/card/12047)), as you won't see it too often. I'd upgrade [Marcus Sengstacke](/card/60375) before buying [Well Connected](/card/60381) when taking this alternate route. In lower XP campaigns though, I prioritize getting the zanier upgrade early - optimization be damned! Post-18 XP suggestions are: - [Out the Door](/card/60370) → [Out the Door •](/card/60373) - 1 x [Silver Tongue](/card/12047) → 1 x [Silver Tongue •••](/card/60380) - [Sticky Fingers](/card/12048) → [Sticky Fingers ••](/card/12054)

Compatability Matrix

Everyone likes a good matrix! Below are all the decks that are compatible at two player using one Chapter 2 Core and one 2026 Starter Deck set: For higher player counts I've not 'compatabilized' the basic skills ([Overpower](/card/12092), [Manual Dexterity](/card/12091), [Guts](/card/12090), [Perception](/card/12093) and [Unexpected Courage](/card/12094)). There are only 4 copies of each in the Chapter 2 core, enough for any two decks. If playing 3+ players and there's a clash, you can either: - Swap with an appropriate level 0 class skill which that deck can use (e.g. [On the Brink](/card/60569) for [Unexpected Courage](/card/12094)). - Swap with a class event or asset with matching or similar symbols (e.g. [Working a Hunch](/card/12038) for [Perception](/card/12093)). - Swap with a different underused basic skill you still believe would be useful for the deck (e.g. [Guts](/card/12090) for [Unexpected Courage](/card/12094)). - Proxy however you see fit (especially if you own Chapter 1 cards, just use the old school versions and remember the slight difference around who draws the card). I empower you to do sensible things!

Final thoughts

While this deck isn't crazy powerful in any one area, it's competent in many - which I think is exactly what you want in an archetypal Rogue (making everything about tests, or money, or both). I know some people call Rogues in this chapter "green Mystics" and, while I can see that a bit, there is some nuance with how Agility works on Rogues - e.g. they do receive innate enemy management, so their assets are weaker vs. a Mystic. This lends itself to a quantity not quality approach, which is further amped up here by André getting an extra action most rounds. The "a lot of little bites" playstyle is a fun one, so for me André is great! Any thoughts - drop them below!
